clue.text: Drugged drink — one's taken around four

definitions.note: a definition by description: the light meal is eaten in the late afternoon, about four o'clock

parts.note: someone drugged is said to be high
tea is the classic British drink

explanation.surface: Someone has spiked a drink, and the culprit is seen hovering around four people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the second half, describing the meal by its time of day; 'around four' reads like a count of people but is a time.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is a British early-evening or late-afternoon meal, traditionally served about four or five o'clock.

clue.text: Revolutionary ill-advised to capture American soldier

indicators.note: to capture means the reversed word holds the American letters
revolutionary says the word for ill-advised turns round

parts.note: rash means reckless, ill-advised
US for United States

explanation.surface: A rash rebel captures an American serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier, originally in the Hungarian army.

clue.text: Festivity offering gratis entry occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters, every other one, are used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebration that sometimes lets people in free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiety is merriment and cheerful celebration, the mood of a festive occasion.

clue.text: Perfect bit of rabbit or cheese served up

parts.note: the tail is a part of a rabbit
taken as written

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the cheese is written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A rabbit morsel or a cheese plate, presented as the ideal dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' is an adjective, meaning exactly suited.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tailor-made is made to fit exactly, so it is perfectly suited to its purpose.

clue.text: In Cancun, take care …

definitions.meaning: Cancun is a Mexican resort, so the farewell is in Spanish
a parting phrase, standing for goodbye

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 5-down, whose Mexican food continues the Cancun theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Adios is Spanish for goodbye, the farewell one would say on leaving someone in Mexico.

clue.text: Former spouse Hello snapped in parade

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
hi is an informal greeting
bit, past tense of bite, as a dog snaps

explanation.surface: A former partner, greeting someone, lashed out during a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parade' is a verb here, meaning to show off, not a march.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to display it openly, which is what exhibiting it means.

clue.text: .. Russian's agreed to support Chilean cooking Mexican food

indicators.note: to support in a down clue means the Russian yes goes underneath, after the rest
cooking means the letters of Chilean are stirred into a new mix

parts.note: taken as written
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: A Russian is happy for a Chilean to cook a Mexican dish, continuing from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a rolled tortilla with a filling, covered in chilli sauce.

clue.text: What that RC priest's sung?

indicators.note: sung says the word is heard, not read, as words of a song are

parts.note: a Roman Catholic priest is male, so the pronoun for that priest is him

explanation.surface: A question about which song a particular Catholic priest has just sung.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the church song sounds the same as the pronoun for that priest; the RC fixes the priest as a man, and the whole clue describes what he sings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise sung in church services.

clue.text: Killers however will get female singer's following

indicators.note: following means the singer's name comes after the word for however

parts.note: but and however both introduce a contrast
Cher is an American female pop singer

explanation.surface: Murderers are about to get a pop diva's fan base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a noun for a fan base; it is the order signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers slaughter animals, and the word is also used for brutal murderers, so it fits killers.

clue.text: Cheers team with cold six-pack — they're handy movers

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as cheers is
XI, eleven, is a football or cricket team
abs, abdominal muscles, form a six-pack

explanation.surface: Toasting a team with a cold six-pack of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-pack' suggests beer cans but means stomach muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxicabs are hire cars that are convenient to flag down and carry passengers about town.

clue.text: Visions of the future if one's looking back over century

indicators.note: looking back says the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: over has the letters of one's spread across the century letter, enclosing it

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one is) is IS
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Imagining the future means looking back over a hundred years, if you are that sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is read as one is, giving I plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is the genre of imagined futures, so its stories are visions of what is to come.

clue.text: We all have to give this latest heavenly streaker a ten

definitions.text: We all have to give this
definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the levy every earner must pay

parts.note: the latest thing is in, fashionable
a comet streaks across the heavens
taken as written
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Everyone must award a top mark of ten to the latest naked runner in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaker' suggests someone running naked; here it is a comet streaking across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Income tax is the levy charged on earnings, which almost every worker must hand over to the state.

clue.text: A universal god's in Genesis

parts.note: taken as written
U is the film certificate for universal viewing
Thor is the Norse god of thunder
hip and in both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A god for everyone appears in the first book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genesis' looks like the Bible book, but it is the definition in its sense of origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means origin or creation, and authorship is the act of originating a piece of work.

clue.text: Elegant and spineless? Not Barbie's boy

indicators.note: not says the boyfriend's name is removed from the word for spineless

parts.note: a coward, someone spineless, is called chicken
Ken is Barbie's doll boyfriend

explanation.surface: A question about whether Barbie's boyfriend is stylish and cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a borrowed French word for stylish, describing someone elegantly fashionable.

clue.text: Dawn, natural when topless, right dare-devil

parts.note: an advent, an arrival, is the dawn of something

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter, its top in a down clue

parts.note: pure means natural, unadulterated

explanation.surface: A daring woman named Dawn goes topless, naturally enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name; it means a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer takes risks seeking excitement, which is what a dare-devil does.

clue.text: Grip used by tennis stroke with shattering action

parts.note: a smash is a hard overhead shot in tennis
and joins things, as with does
to grab is to grip

explanation.surface: A tennis player's grip is used for a smash that breaks something.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read out of clue order: the stroke comes first and the grip last.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-and-grab is a robbery in which a thief breaks a shop window and snatches goods.

clue.text: Colossal VAT I only charged with delivering

definitions.note: a noun phrase for rescue, delivering from harm, standing for the noun answer

indicators.note: charged with, like loaded with, says the words carry the answer within them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge sales tax bill is the only thing a supplier is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvation is deliverance from sin or danger, the act of delivering someone from harm.

clue.text: Plot climb with no railings above a South American city

indicators.note: above in a down clue means the first part sits over the rest
with no railings means the word loses its outer letters, its edges

parts.note: ascend means climb
taken as written
Rio de Janeiro, in Brazil

explanation.surface: A climb with no safety railings above a city in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of a story's events, which is what its plot is.

clue.text: A few runs laid down for county

parts.note: some means a few
set means laid down, placed

explanation.surface: A few cricket runs are scored for the county side.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England, with a county cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county in the south-west, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: Fans' favourite collection, Requests by Queen

parts.note: a crowd is a collection of people
pleas are requests
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A royal compilation of listener requests becomes the fans' top album.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd-pleaser is a performer or item that wins popular approval, so it is what an audience loves.

clue.text: Poser put out consuming Double Diamonds

indicators.note: consuming means the word for annoy holds the diamonds inside

parts.note: to put someone out is to annoy, or rile, them
D is diamonds in card notation, so two diamonds is DD; Double Diamond is also a British beer

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed while drinking Double Diamond, a British bitter beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question, and a riddle is a puzzle set as a question.

clue.text: Wrong place to leave butts — not around hospital

indicators.note: not around says the hospital letter is no longer present in the word

parts.note: an ashtray is where cigarette ends are stubbed out
H as on a road sign

explanation.surface: A smoker is told that the wrong place to drop cigarette ends is near a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butts' are cigarette ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone astray means gone off course, so astray is used for being in the wrong or mistaken.

clue.text: When it's said we might see Santa Caus?

definitions.text: When it's said we might see Santa Caus?

indicators.note: when it's said means the letters are spoken aloud, and what matters is how they sound

parts.note: Santa Claus printed with no L, which spoken is the sound of the answer

explanation.surface: A seasonal question about when Father Christmas, misspelt, is likely to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The apparent typo is deliberate: Caus is Claus with no L, and 'no L' spoken is the Christmas word; the whole clue also describes the season when Santa comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the time of year Father Christmas is expected to visit.

clue.text: Striptease disguised dangling items on display

indicators.note: disguised means the letters of the word striptease appear in a different form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A striptease in disguise, with something hanging out for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cheeky; the definition is innocent wall hangings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestries are woven textile pictures that are hung on walls for show.

clue.text: Scoffed hearing school's announcement

indicators.note: hearing says the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling
an announcement is something spoken out, so the school's name is heard rather than read

parts.note: Eton is the famous English boarding school

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked on hearing a school's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mocked; it means gobbled up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is British slang for eating greedily, so scoffed food has been eaten.

clue.text: Show off clothes for climbing

indicators.note: for climbing in a down clue means the word for clothes reads upwards, in reverse

parts.note: garb is clothing

explanation.surface: Flaunting one's climbing gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, which is to show off about oneself.

clue.text: Prudence makes entry in Pierre's train timetable

indicators.note: makes entry in says the answer has entered these words and sits within them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A careful Frenchman's name is added to the railway schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint means self-control and moderation, which is close to the sense of prudence as caution.

clue.text: Perhaps biker I unseated by university will become more offensive

indicators.note: unseated by says the I loses its place, replaced by the university letter

parts.note: a biker is one example of a rider
taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist thrown off by a college gets increasingly rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks biker as an example of a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruder is the comparative of rude, so it means more offensive or impolite.

clue.text: Geometrical shape that's like the quarter-finals?

definitions.meaning: the plain meaning: a flat figure with straight sides
the quarter-finals involve eight competitors, and the shape has eight sides

explanation.walkthrough: The quarter-finals are the stage with eight teams left; the octagon is also the eight-sided cage used in mixed martial arts.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a polygon with eight sides, matching the eight sides left at the quarter-final stage.

clue.text: Go back by Southeastern Trains, making room for kids

indicators.note: back says the word for go is read in reverse

parts.note: to run is to go
RY, railway, the abbreviation for a line carrying trains

explanation.surface: A commuter retreats on the Southeastern line, freeing a space for children.
explanation.walkthrough: Southeastern is a real London commuter train operator, so the surface reads as a rail journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a room in a house set aside for babies and young children.
